q: In Grade 11, the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular ____ of an object in circular motion have been learnt.
e: The textbook lists angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration as the rotational variables learnt in Grade 11.

q: In Grade 11, the angular ____, angular velocity and angular acceleration of an object in circular motion have been learnt.
e: Angular displacement is the first of the three rotational variables introduced in Grade 11.

q: In this chapter, the concepts and equations for rotational motion under constant angular acceleration and ____ acceleration will be studied.
e: The chapter focuses on rotational motion under constant angular acceleration and centripetal acceleration.

q: It is expected that students will differentiate between the circular motion and ____ motion.
e: Differentiating between circular and rotational motion is a key learning outcome of the chapter.

q: It is expected that students will examine rotational motion under constant angular ____.
e: Examining rotational motion under constant angular acceleration is a stated learning outcome.

q: It is expected that students will deduce the relations between angular and ____ quantities.
e: Students are expected to deduce the relations between angular and linear quantities.

q: It is expected that students will understand the ____ acceleration.
e: Understanding centripetal acceleration is one of the core learning outcomes.

q: It is expected that students will distinguish between the uniform circular motion and ____ circular motion.
e: Distinguishing between uniform and nonuniform circular motion is a key learning outcome.

q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a ____.
e: The textbook defines circular motion as an object just moving in a circle.

q: Artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height is an example of ____ motion.
e: Artificial satellites orbiting the earth are given as an example of circular motion.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an ____.
e: Rotational motion is defined as an object rotating about an axis.

q: The rotation of earth about its own axis creates the cycle of day and ____.
e: The earth's rotation about its axis creates the cycle of day and night.

q: The motion of the blades of a ____ is an example of rotational motion.
e: The motion of fan blades is listed as an example of rotational motion.

q: The motion of a ____ wheel in an amusement park is an example of rotational motion.
e: A Ferris wheel in an amusement park is given as an example of rotational motion.

q: A ____ body is a body that does not deform or change shape.
e: A rigid body is defined as a body that does not deform or change shape.

q: That is, no matter how the body moves, the ____ between any two particles within the body remains constant.
e: For a rigid body, the distance between any two particles remains constant regardless of its motion.

q: For a rigid body, the distance between any two ____ within the body remains constant.
e: The constant distance applies to any two particles constituting the rigid body.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo ____ motion about a common axis.
e: All particles of a rigid body in rotational motion undergo circular motion about a common axis.

q: When an object (rigid body) rotates, it can speed up or slow ____.
e: A rotating rigid body can change its speed by speeding up or slowing down.

q: During these time intervals, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular ____.
e: A changing angular velocity means the object possesses an angular acceleration.

q: If its angular velocity changes at a constant rate, then we can say that the angular acceleration is constant and the motion is called the rotational motion under constant angular ____.
e: Motion with a constant rate of change in angular velocity is called rotational motion under constant angular acceleration.

q: Angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are examples of ____ variables.
e: These three quantities are classified as rotational variables.

q: Rotational variables are applied to analyze the rotational motion for a rigid body about a fixed ____ under a constant angular acceleration.
e: The analysis in this section focuses on a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis.

q: For an object that rotates with a constant angular acceleration, the ____ equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant of time.
e: Kinematic equations are derived for rotational motion under constant angular acceleration.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t = $ ____.
e: Initial angular speed is defined at time $t=0$.

q: The equation for angular speed is $\omega = \omega_0 + $ ____.
e: This is the kinematic equation relating final angular speed, initial angular speed, angular acceleration, and time.

q: Average angular speed is, $\frac{\omega + \omega_0}{____}$.
e: The average angular speed is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final angular speeds.

q: The equation for angular displacement is $\theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2} $ ____.
e: This is the kinematic equation for angular displacement under constant angular acceleration.

q: The relation between angular speed and angular displacement is $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + $ ____.
e: This is the time-independent kinematic equation for rotational motion.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are the same as those for linear motion, with the angular quantities replaced with corresponding ____ ones.
e: The rotational kinematic equations are direct analogues of the linear kinematic equations.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in ____ motion.
e: Table 1.1 shows the direct analogy between linear and angular kinematic equations.
